newsitem.title: DUBAI: UAE drops McDonnell Douglas from $6 bln plane deal.
newsitem.headline: UAE drops McDonnell Douglas from $6 bln plane deal.

text.p: The United Arab Emirates has officially told the United States of its interest in the F-16 Block 60 warplane in a deal possibly worth $6 billion, dropping the rival U.S. F-15 but keeping the French Rafale in the contest, official military sources said on Wednesday.

A senior UAE official told Reuters McDonnell Douglas Corp's F-15 was taken out of the contest for up to 80 warplanes, with Lockheed Martin Corp, also of the United States, and France's Dassault Aviation the remaining bidders.
"From the American offers we have picked the F-16 over the F-15," he added.

The UAE "is still interested in a small added number of (French) Mirage 2000s and also looking at the Rafale as a competitor to the F-16," said the official who is close to the negotiations for the deal which could be the last of its size this century.

UAE officials said the Gulf Arab state would not request further in-country trials by competing aircraft, adding that the selection process in the long-awaited, fiercely contested deal could take another "few months."
